evidence.positive: Against the running app (localhost:62476, image guidedclinical/orci:loop-e7eeafd6c, which contains the fix commit bfe0654a7 as an ancestor), logged in as admin and called the endpoint from the Sentry stack, GET /api/admin/observations/patient/or2680-does-not-exist/ with X-Tenant-Id: demo-demo. Observed HTTP 404: {"timestamp":"2026-08-24T21:19:18.830+00:00","status":404,"error":"Not Found","message":"Patient not found","path":"/api/admin/observations/patient/or2680-does-not-exist/"}. Repeated with X-Tenant-Id: mayo-mayo, also 404 "Patient not found". The container log slice captured across those requests contains zero occurrences of NullPointerException (grep -c NullPointerException = 0), i.e. no 500 and no PatientService.getObservations frame.
evidence.negative: Verified the new guard does not fire for a patient that does exist, so the 404 is not blanket behaviour. Created a real patient via POST /api/admin/patients/ (pmrn or2680-fake-f3a8dd64-b2ad-459d-8567-481a5f6df4e5, uuid 01a035a2-7f29-7ca7-ad5d-c2934ae61b41), created an operation (caseId 15182, p-appendectomy), and added a GLUCOSE observation via POST /api/admin/observations/patient/{pmrn}/case/15182 (200). GET /api/admin/observations/patient/or2680-fake-f3a8dd64-b2ad-459d-8567-481a5f6df4e5/ returned HTTP 200 with [{"id":"01a035a2-7f66-73ce-a483-e6ac69bb00c1",...,"observationValue":"137","observationUnits":"mg/dL","type":"GLUCOSE"}] — patient.getId() was dereferenced successfully and the real observation list came back, so PatientNotFoundException was NOT thrown.
evidence.red_check: Ran the pre-fix code in the live container. Took orci/src/main/java/com/guided/orci/web/admin/ObservationController.java at bfe0654a7^ (identical to shipped except the three-line null guard), removed the unused @Slf4j annotation/import so it compiles without lombok on the runtime classpath, compiled it inside the container with javac -parameters -cp $(cat /app/jib-classpath-file), confirmed via javap that getObservations goes straight from PatientService.getPatient to PatientService.getObservations with no null branch, backed up the shipped classes (md5 caafa822429eaf60faf885ff270aa574 for ObservationController.class, 4fcfba75ff6da7f76b610424a5d9dd0b for ObservationController$AddObservationDTO.class, copies also kept on the host), swapped the pre-fix classes into /app/classes and restarted the container. The app booted normally ("Started OrciApplication in 11.54 seconds"). The same unknown-patient request then went RED: HTTP 500 with message "Cannot invoke \"com.guided.orci.models.patient.Patient.getId()\" because \"patient\" is null", and the container log printed java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "com.guided.orci.models.patient.Patient.getId()" because "patient" is null / at com.guided.orci.service.PatientService.getObservations(PatientService.java:202) / at com.guided.orci.web.admin.ObservationController.getObservations(ObservationController.java:122) — the same two frames as the Sentry report. The existing-patient request still returned 200 under the pre-fix class, confirming the only behavioural difference is the unknown-patient path. Then restored the backed-up shipped classes and restarted: md5sums match the pre-swap values exactly (caafa822429eaf60faf885ff270aa574 / 4fcfba75ff6da7f76b610424a5d9dd0b), the unknown-patient request is 404 again, the existing-patient request is 200 with the glucose observation again, and the post-restore log slice has zero NullPointerException occurrences.

caveats: Only the admin REST endpoint was exercised; there is no user-facing UI route for GET /api/admin/observations/patient/{pmrn}/ that was driven end to end.
The pre-fix class used for the red check was recompiled with @Slf4j stripped (the class contains no log usage) rather than being extracted from a pre-fix image build.
Tenants exercised were demo-demo (full positive/negative) and mayo-mayo (404 only); no MGB tenant was touched.
The sibling endpoints on ObservationController (addObservation, delete paths) were only exercised incidentally during setup, not re-validated after the class restore.

automation.assessment: The fix commit already ships orci/src/test/java/com/guided/orci/web/admin/ObservationControllerTest.java, which covers both the null-patient path (asserts PatientNotFoundException) and the happy path (asserts mapped DTOs). That is adequate unit-level coverage of the guard itself. The one gap is that the test asserts the exception type, not the HTTP status — the 404 comes from @ResponseStatus on PatientNotFoundException, which the unit test never exercises. A thin web-layer test would lock in the contract the ticket actually cares about (404 rather than 500). No qa-suite work is warranted for an admin-only debug endpoint.
proposed_tests: MockMvc (standaloneSetup or @WebMvcTest) test asserting GET /api/admin/observations/patient/{unknown}/ responds 404 with message "Patient not found", so the @ResponseStatus mapping is covered and a regression to 500 fails the build.
Companion MockMvc case asserting GET for an existing patient responds 200 with the observation list, guarding against the guard over-triggering.

jira_comment:
Validated against a throwaway instance built from e7eeafd6c (contains the fix commit bfe0654a7). Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: GET /api/admin/observations/patient/or2680-does-not-exist/ on the demo tenant returned HTTP 404 with "Patient not found" instead of a 500, and the container log showed no NullPointerException. Same result on the mayo tenant.

Negative: a real patient was created with a GLUCOSE observation attached, and GET on that patient returned HTTP 200 with the observation (value 137 mg/dL), confirming the new null guard does not fire for patients that exist.

Red check: the pre-fix version of ObservationController was compiled and swapped into /app/classes in the running container. The same unknown-patient request then returned HTTP 500 with 'Cannot invoke com.guided.orci.models.patient.Patient.getId() because patient is null', with the identical PatientService.getObservations / ObservationController.getObservations frames from the Sentry report. The shipped classes were restored, checksums confirmed to match, the app restarted, and both the 404 and the 200 cases were re-run clean.

Automation: the fix commit already includes a unit test covering the null path and the happy path. Proposed follow-up is a thin MockMvc test asserting the HTTP status is 404 rather than only the exception type, since the 404 comes from the @ResponseStatus mapping that the unit test does not exercise.
